title: Toward Valid Generative Clinical Trial Data with Survival Endpoints
summary: Generates synthetic control arms for late-phase oncology and rare-disease trials by learning covariates and the time-to-event endpoint jointly in one latent variational model rather than in the two-stage pipeline the GAN-based survival generators use, so that censoring and small sample sizes are handled inside the generative model instead of by a separate downstream time regressor. TVAE runs inside the comparison: the Surv-VAE arm is the SurvivalGAN pipeline with its GAN covariate module replaced by the tabular variational autoencoder of Xu et al., while CTGAN and TVAE as standalone generators were considered and excluded on the strength of SurvivalGAN's earlier finding that they are less effective for survival modelling.

evidence: the related-work section names TGAN, TVAE (Xu et al. 2019) and CTAB-GAN among the data-driven generative models applied to tabular clinical datasets; section 3.2 states that other tabular data generators such as CTGAN, TVAE or normalizing flows were compared to SurvivalGAN in Norcliffe et al. 2023 and found less effective for survival modelling, and were therefore excluded from this paper's comparison, leaving Surv-GAN and Surv-VAE as the two competing methods; appendix A.1 states that SurvivalVAE adopts the same pipeline framework as SurvivalGAN, replacing the GAN module with a Tabular Variational Autoencoder (Xu et al. 2019) to generate covariates. Importance 3: TVAE is executed as the covariate generator inside one of the two compared methods rather than benchmarked directly, and none of CTGAN's conditional vector or mode-specific normalization is adopted.

title: PluRel: Synthetic Data unlocks Scaling Laws for Relational Foundation Models
summary: Synthesizes whole multi-table relational databases from scratch rather than imitating an existing one, modelling schemas as directed graphs, primary-foreign key connectivity as bipartite graphs and per-table feature distributions through conditional causal mechanisms, and uses the resulting unlimited supply of databases to show that relational foundation model pretraining loss follows power-law scaling in both the number of synthetic databases and total tokens, with the gains transferring zero-shot to real benchmarks. The Synthetic Data Vault is the named prior art the framework departs from: it is cited for the premise that relational databases are rarely public because they hold sensitive information, and again as the privacy-preserving relational generator that reproduces the structure and statistics of a given real database but cannot produce novel ones from scratch.
evidence: the introduction states that relational databases are rarely public because they typically contain sensitive user or enterprise information, citing Patki et al. 2016; the related-work section names privacy-preserving synthetic database generation, citing Patki et al. 2016, as a line of research focused on reproducing the structure and statistical properties of a given real-world database while protecting data subjects; the method motivation states that alternative approaches such as the Synthetic Data Vault (Patki et al. 2016), GAN-based and diffusion models can capture characteristics of real-world databases but cannot generate novel ones from scratch without relying on existing real-world examples, which is the limitation the framework is introduced to address. The tight scan returns one hit in the whole PDF and it resolves to the SDV anchor paper, not to CTGAN; nothing SDV-family is run. Importance 2 rather than 1 under the convention for prior art a paper departs from: SDV is named individually in three places with a stated limitation, not listed undifferentiated.

title: Bayesian Generative Adversarial Networks via Gaussian Approximation for Tabular Data Synthesis
summary: Places a Bayesian posterior over a tabular GAN's generator weights without the memory cost of the Markov chain approach, by collecting a running mean and low-rank plus diagonal covariance of the generator weights during training with Stochastic Weight Averaging-Gaussian and sampling from that Gaussian at synthesis time, and reports on five national census tables plus Adult and a churn dataset that the result sits higher on the utility axis of a risk-utility map without a matching rise in attribute-disclosure risk. The model is a named CTGAN variant: SWAG is integrated into CTGAN's own generator, the paper's ablations run averaging-only and several covariance ranks against unmodified CTGAN and a Markov-chain BayesCTGAN, and the implementation is published as a CTGAN fork.
evidence: the abstract introduces Gaussian Approximation of CTGAN (GACTGAN) as an integration of SWAG within the CTGAN generator and states it yields better synthetic data compared to CTGAN; the introduction credits CTGAN (Xu et al. 2019) with addressing heterogeneous tabular features by modelling conditional distributions and using training-by-sampling; the contributions list names GACTGAN as putting a Bayesian posterior over the generator and section 4.2.2 defines the variants, including an averaging-only ACTGAN and diagonal and low-rank covariance settings; the complexity discussion compares the training cost directly against the baseline CTGAN complexity; Figures 2, 4, 6 and 7 report CTGAN, BayesCTGAN, ACTGAN and four GACTGAN configurations side by side under Wasserstein and vanilla losses on the UK, Indonesia, Canada, Fiji and Rwanda census tables plus Adult and Churn; the data and code availability statement gives github.com/rulnasution/ctgan-bayes. The variant name appears in the title and abstract, unlike the majority of derivatives found in this project.

title: ReTabSyn: Realistic Tabular Data Synthesis via Reinforcement Learning
summary: Fine-tunes a language-model tabular generator with reinforcement learning against a reward built from feature-target correlation preservation, on the argument that matching the full joint distribution is unnecessary and data-hungry when downstream utility is bounded by feature mismatch and conditional-distribution mismatch alone, and reports gains over interpolation, diffusion, autoregressive and other RL-guided generators in low-sample, class-imbalanced and distribution-shifted regimes. SDV appears on both sides of the evaluation: TVAE is run from the official SDV library implementation at its default settings as one of six baselines, and the Shape and Corr. columns of the fidelity table are SDMetrics measures, with marginal similarity aggregated from Kolmogorov-Smirnov and total-variation scores and pairwise correlation similarity computed with contingency similarity for categorical pairs and a mixed-type method, cited to DataCebo's Synthetic Data Metrics.
evidence: appendix D states for the TVAE baseline (Xu et al. 2019) that the authors used the official SDV library implementation and lists its default parameters, class dimensions (256, 256, 256, 256), random dimensions 100, 64 channels, l2scale 1e-5, batch size 500, 300 epochs; the baselines paragraph in section 4.1 lists TVAE among SMOTE, TabSyn, GReaT, PTA and SynRL; appendix I defines the fidelity metrics, aggregating 1-KS for numerical and 1-TVD for categorical columns as Shape and computing pairwise correlation similarity with Pearson for numeric pairs, contingency similarity for categorical pairs and a mixed-type method for numeric-categorical, cited to DataCebo Inc., Synthetic Data Metrics, docs.sdv.dev/sdmetrics version 0.12.0, and Table 4 reports those Shape and Corr. columns for every model. Beware a scan trap here: most of this paper's 'Xu et al.' hits are Xu et al. 2023, the downstream-utility bound, not Xu et al. 2019. Importance 4 on the DP-CGANS precedent that running an SDV-family tool outranks a comparison role, SDMetrics supplying one of five results tables; a reviewer applying the CALIME and Data-IQ precedent instead would record 3.
